Chapter.description: A group of Scenes under one heading: a chapter of the video.
Chapter.deviation: It organises the review and the video's chapters only; it has no machine and no events.
Chapter.origin: Fountain 1.1, Section (`# Title`); no statechart construct

WordAnchor.description: The start of a word, or of the first word of a phrase, or the end of its last word, in this Scene's narration.
WordAnchor.deviation: A word is a source, not a machine: its times come from the alignment of the speech, and a phrase must stay within one Line.
WordAnchor.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, event-value on a media marker (a word of the narration is a sync point)

PercentPoint.description: N percent of the way through a transition's window.
PercentPoint.deviation: N% is the threshold of a progress behaviour from 0 to 1 (eased for a move and an update, linear in time otherwise), not an offset in time; an instant has no percent.
PercentPoint.origin: Fran (Elliott and Hudak 1997), an event taken from a behaviour: when(progress >= N%)

Point.description: A point of a transition: its start, its end, or N percent of the way.
Point.deviation: A transition is a declared machine edge with a window, so a point is a frame of that window.
Point.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, syncbase-value (id.begin, id.end); Fran (Elliott and Hudak 1997), progress threshold

ElementSubject.description: An Element of the Scene, by id.
ElementSubject.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, the element id of a syncbase-value; SCXML state id

EffectSubject.description: An effect of the Scene, by id.
EffectSubject.deviation: Effect ids are local to their Scene.
EffectSubject.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, the element id of a timed child

SceneSubject.description: The Scene itself: its slide change and its end.
SceneSubject.origin: SCXML, the enclosing compound <state>; SMIL 3.0 timing, the time container

StateSubject.description: The n-th State of the Scene, counted from 1.
StateSubject.deviation: States are not declared: the engine derives them from the step frames, one more State for each show or focus.
StateSubject.origin: Harel 1987, State (a node that holds for a dwell interval)

BeatSubject.description: The n-th Beat of the Scene, counted from 1: the transition from State n to State n+1.
BeatSubject.deviation: A Beat is generated from each distinct fire frame of a show or focus after the Scene's first frame, and lasts as long as the slowest step that fires then.
BeatSubject.origin: Harel 1987, the transition between two States; Mealy machine outputs

Subject.description: Who an anchor is about: an Element, an effect, the Scene, a State or a Beat.
Subject.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, the element id a syncbase-value refers to; SCXML state ids

EdgeAnchor.description: A point of a transition of a machine of the subject.
EdgeAnchor.deviation: The spellings are generated from the declared machines; start and end are the first and last frame of the transition's window, N% by the declared easing for a move and an update.
EdgeAnchor.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, syncbase-value (id.begin, id.end); Harel 1987, the start and end of a transition; Fran (Elliott and Hudak 1997), progress

OccupancyAnchor.description: The first frame a machine of the subject enters or leaves a state.
OccupancyAnchor.deviation: A state is left at the slide change at the latest, so a state still held leaves at the Scene's last frame; a state the Scene never reaches has no event.
OccupancyAnchor.origin: Harel 1987, entry and exit of a state (Moore machine outputs); SCXML onentry and onexit

Anchor.description: A moment of the story an effect can wait for: a word, a point of a transition, or a state entered or left.
Anchor.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, syncbase-value and event-value; Harel 1987, events of a statechart

RefEvent.description: The event of a `let` line, by name.
RefEvent.deviation: Local to its Scene and evaluated once; a name that waits for itself is a lint error.
RefEvent.origin: Fran (Elliott and Hudak 1997), a named event; RxJS share (explanatory only)

LastEvent.description: Happens when every operand has happened.
LastEvent.deviation: At the last occurrence of every operand; it never happens while one operand never does.
LastEvent.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, endsync="last"; RxJS forkJoin (explanatory only)

FirstEvent.description: Happens at the earliest of the operands.
FirstEvent.deviation: The earliest first occurrence among the operands that have one.
FirstEvent.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, endsync="first"; RxJS race (explanatory only)

Duration.description: A length of time that is never a share of a window: the gap of throttle and of stagger.
Duration.deviation: Strictly positive, in flicks or output frames.
Duration.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, clock value (dur); RxJS throttleTime and delay (explanatory only)

EachEvent.description: Happens at every occurrence of every operand, optionally thinned by throttle or spaced by stagger.
EachEvent.deviation: Only an each can have several occurrences, and then a sound runs once for each; throttle keeps the leading occurrence and stagger pushes later ones apart, neither of which SMIL has.
EachEvent.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, begin-value list; RxJS merge, throttle (explanatory only)

WithinEvent.description: The occurrences of an event that fall inside the dwell of State n.
WithinEvent.deviation: Both ends of the dwell interval count as inside.
WithinEvent.origin: Harel 1987, a State as scope (an event counts only while the State holds)

TimeOffset.description: A signed time added to every occurrence of an event.
TimeOffset.deviation: In exact flicks (1/705,600,000 s), never milliseconds; f is output frames at the Plan's rate; a time becomes the nearest frame, a half going to the later one (floor(t x rate + 1/2)).

PercentOffset.description: A signed share of the window of the event it is added to.
PercentOffset.deviation: It needs a window: an event that is an instant has none, and the percent is an error.

Offset.description: A signed offset from an event: a time or a share of its window.

ShiftEvent.description: Every occurrence of an event moved by an offset.
ShiftEvent.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, offset-value on a begin value

EventExpr.description: A finite list of moments, built from anchors and combinators; it resolves to frames at plan time.
EventExpr.deviation: Every combinator is a total function from finite lists of frames to a list of frames; an empty result is an error only where an effect needs a moment.
EventExpr.origin: Fran (Elliott and Hudak 1997), the event algebra; SMIL 3.0 timing, begin-value list

Until.description: The event that ends an effect with a duration.
Until.deviation: Only on a focus (a show stays shown and a sound plays out); the end is the first occurrence strictly after the fire frame; an event that comes later than the Scene, or never, leaves the effect to the slide change.
Until.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, end value; RxJS takeUntil (explanatory only)

EventWhen.description: The effect fires at each occurrence of an event.

AbsoluteWhen.description: The effect fires a fixed time after the slide change of its Scene.
AbsoluteWhen.deviation: Exact flicks, never milliseconds; it needs a reason, which lint lists.
AbsoluteWhen.origin: SMIL 3.0 timing, offset-value (a clock value from the begin of the parent)

When.description: What the author wrote for the timing of an effect: an event, or a fixed time with its reason.

Effect.description: A sound, a show or a focus, and when it happens. SMIL attributes of each verb (declared once per verb in grammar.ts, not stored per effect): restart overlap for every verb; fill freeze for a show, remove for a focus and a sound.
Effect.deviation: restart: overlap, which is not a SMIL value: an effect with several occurrences of its begin event runs once for each (only a sound may), and instances do not restart each other, unlike SMIL restart="always"; occurrences of one event at the same frame are one occurrence; the slide change ends every running effect.
Effect.origin: Mealy and Moore machine outputs (an effect subscribes to a transition or to a state's enter or leave); SMIL 3.0 timing, a timed child with a begin and an end

Element.description: A thing on the slide, with a cell, a class and a text; its id is its identity across Scenes.
Element.deviation: The regions are declared once as machines, and their transitions come from the identity diff between two Scenes (the same id is the same Element), not from authored events.
Element.origin: Harel 1987, orthogonality (presence, position and style are parallel regions of one Element); SCXML <parallel>

DerivedEvent.description: A `let` line: a name for an event of the Scene, evaluated once and used wherever the name is written.
DerivedEvent.deviation: Local to its Scene; a name that waits for itself is a lint error.
DerivedEvent.origin: Fran (Elliott and Hudak 1997), a named event; RxJS share (explanatory only)

LineHints.description: How the narrator says a Line: the pause before it and the speed.
LineHints.deviation: A speed is a multiple of the voice's natural rate between 0.5 and 2, not a percent.

Line.description: One thing the narrator says in a Scene: its text, spoken word by word.
Line.deviation: The text is byte-identical across revisions of a Story so the speech cache keeps hitting; the times of its words come from alignment, never from the author.
Line.origin: Fountain 1.1, Dialogue of NARRATOR; SMIL 3.0 timing, a media element (its words are sync points)

GraphScene.description: A Scene as declared: its Elements, Lines, effects and derived events.
GraphScene.deviation: The States inside a Scene are not declared: the engine derives them from the step frames; the identity diff against the previous Scene is derived, not declared; a Scene is left at its last frame, which ends every effect running in it.
GraphScene.origin: Harel 1987, depth (a Scene is a compound State, a superstate of its States); SCXML compound <state>; SMIL 3.0 timing, a time container whose end ends its children

Graph.description: The IR of a Story: the state and beat graph, as a closed, versioned document.
Graph.deviation: Closed (an excess key is a decode error) and versioned (an other version is a decode error); the machines are declared once in the engine, a Story declares only its Scenes, Elements, Lines and effects.
Graph.origin: SCXML 1.0, <scxml> root; Harel 1987, statecharts (a hierarchy of States with orthogonal regions)
